title: Two bands
prompt: Show each employee's name and a band: High for salaries of at least 90000, otherwise Other. Name it band and replace the ___.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test'); UPDATE employees SET salary = 90000 WHERE id = 12;

solutions: SELECT name, CASE WHEN salary >= 90000 THEN 'High' ELSE 'Other' END AS band FROM employees;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, CASE WHEN salary > 90000 THEN 'High' ELSE 'Other' END AS band FROM employees;
SELECT name, CASE WHEN salary >= 90000 THEN 'High' END AS band FROM employees;

title: Zero for missing
prompt: Show each employee's name and their bonus, with missing bonuses shown as 0, as bonus.
hints: COALESCE returns the first non-NULL value.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name, COALESCE(bonus, 0) AS bonus FROM employees;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, COALESCE(bonus, 1) AS bonus FROM employees;

title: Three price bands
prompt: Show each product's name and a price_band: Budget under 5, Mid from 5 up to but not including 30, otherwise Premium.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL); UPDATE products SET price = 5.0 WHERE id = 8; UPDATE products SET price = 30.0 WHERE id = 9;

solutions: SELECT name, CASE WHEN price < 5 THEN 'Budget' WHEN price < 30 THEN 'Mid' ELSE 'Premium' END AS price_band FROM products;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, CASE WHEN price < 30 THEN 'Mid' WHEN price < 5 THEN 'Budget' ELSE 'Premium' END AS price_band FROM products;
wrongSolutions.why: The first match wins, so Budget never appears

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, CASE WHEN price <= 5 THEN 'Budget' WHEN price <= 30 THEN 'Mid' ELSE 'Premium' END AS price_band FROM products;

title: Rain report
prompt: Show each reading's id and a label named report: Unknown if rainfall is missing, Dry if it's 0, otherwise Wet.
solutions: SELECT id, CASE WHEN rainfall_mm IS NULL THEN 'Unknown' WHEN rainfall_mm = 0 THEN 'Dry' ELSE 'Wet' END AS report FROM readings;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, CASE WHEN rainfall_mm = 0 THEN 'Dry' ELSE 'Wet' END AS report FROM readings;
SELECT id, CASE WHEN rainfall_mm = NULL THEN 'Unknown' WHEN rainfall_mm = 0 THEN 'Dry' ELSE 'Wet' END AS report FROM readings;

title: No ELSE
prompt: Show each employee's name and a flag named has_bonus containing Yes when their bonus is above 0. With no ELSE, other rows are NULL, and that's what's wanted.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name, CASE WHEN bonus > 0 THEN 'Yes' END AS has_bonus FROM employees;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, CASE WHEN bonus > 0 THEN 'Yes' ELSE 'No' END AS has_bonus FROM employees;
SELECT name, CASE WHEN bonus >= 0 THEN 'Yes' END AS has_bonus FROM employees;

title: Fix the CASE
prompt: This should label each employee as Senior if hired before 2020, otherwise Junior, in a column named level, but it fails. Fix it.
hints: Every CASE needs a closing END.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM employees; DELETE FROM departments; INSERT INTO departments VALUES (5, 'Design'), (6, 'Finance'), (7, 'Ops'); INSERT INTO employees VALUES (11, 'Ivy', 5, NULL, 90000, '2019-02-01', 900, 'ivy@acme.test'), (12, 'Jon', 5, 11, 70000, '2020-06-15', NULL, NULL), (13, 'Kim', 6, 11, 70000, '2023-03-03', 300, 'kim@acme.test'), (14, 'Leo', NULL, 77, 30000, '2024-08-20', NULL, 'leo@acme.test'), (15, 'Mia', 6, 13, 55000, '2022-12-31', 0, 'mia@acme.test');

solutions: SELECT name, CASE WHEN hire_date < '2020-01-01' THEN 'Senior' ELSE 'Junior' END AS level FROM employees;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT name, CASE WHEN hire_date > '2020-01-01' THEN 'Senior' ELSE 'Junior' END AS level FROM employees;
SELECT name, CASE WHEN hire_date < '2020-01-01' THEN 'Senior' END AS level FROM employees;

title: Best way to reach
prompt: Show each contact's id and their best contact detail as reach: their email if present, else their phone, else the text none.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM contacts; INSERT INTO contacts VALUES (11, 'mary jackson', 'mary-j@club.test', '555-0111', 'Hampton', 'SILVER GOLD1'), (12, 'BOB Kahn', 'bob@CLUB.test', '555-0112', NULL, 'gold1'), (13, 'Rosa Park', 'rosa@club-test', NULL, 'Tuskegee', 'NEW'), (14, 'Ken Thompson', 'ken.t@club.test', '5550114', 'Murray', 'GOLD3');

solutions: SELECT id, COALESCE(email, phone, 'none') AS reach FROM contacts;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, COALESCE(phone, email, 'none') AS reach FROM contacts;
SELECT id, COALESCE(email, 'none') AS reach FROM contacts;

title: Priority order
prompt: Show each order's id and status, with pending orders first, then shipped, then cancelled. Within a status, sort by id.
hints: A CASE can go inside ORDER BY.

cases.name: Different data
cases.setupSql: DELETE FROM order_items; DELETE FROM orders; DELETE FROM products; DELETE FROM customers; INSERT INTO customers VALUES (7, 'Ravi', 'Oslo', 'ravi@mail.test', '2024-05-05'), (8, 'Sara', 'Lima', NULL, '2024-06-06'), (9, 'Tom', 'Oslo', NULL, '2024-07-07'); INSERT INTO products VALUES (7, 'Stool', 'Home', 40.0, 25.0), (8, 'Cup', 'Kitchen', 9.0, 2.0), (9, 'Ink', 'Stationery', 12.5, 6.0); INSERT INTO orders VALUES (11, 7, '2024-02-28', 'shipped'), (12, 8, '2024-03-01', 'pending'), (13, 7, '2024-03-31', 'cancelled'); INSERT INTO order_items VALUES (11, 7, 1, 4.0), (11, 8, 3, NULL), (12, 9, 2, NULL), (13, 8, 1, NULL);

solutions: SELECT id, status FROM orders ORDER BY CASE WHEN status = 'pending' THEN 1 WHEN status = 'shipped' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END, id;

wrongSolutions.sql: SELECT id, status FROM orders ORDER BY status, id;
SELECT id, status FROM orders ORDER BY CASE WHEN status = 'shipped' THEN 1 WHEN status = 'pending' THEN 2 ELSE 3 END, id;
